description: Selection 'd' - LOWER CASE - on row 10: the tenth and last arm of the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :151-185, and the fourth clause of the selection EVALUATE at :189-215. SEL0001I through SEL0009I are every one of them blank, so the nine arms at :152-178 are each evaluated and each found FALSE and only :179-181 matches - MOVE SEL0010I TO CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG and MOVE USRID10I TO CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED. Together with case13, whose tick is on row 1, this spans the full width of the ten-way scan, which is what makes its ORDER observable rather than merely asserted (gate G30): a scan that consulted the ten cells in any other order, or that took the last tick rather than the first, could not answer this page the way the source does. USRID10I is USER0005, the tenth identifier of page 1, and the tenth arm exists at all because the page holds ten rows - which is BEHAVIOUR and not configuration (gate G39), hard-coded at :293, :300, :347 and :352 and by 02 USER-REC OCCURS 10 TIMES at :57, and appearing nowhere in this file as a tunable. THE CASE OF THE CHARACTER IS PRESERVED, and that is the second property this case exists to pin. There is no FUNCTION UPPER-CASE anywhere in app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl, so :180 stores the character exactly as the operator typed it and CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG leaves holding a lower-case 'd'. app/bms/COUSR00.bms:446-447 paints 'Type ''U'' to Update or ''D'' to Delete a User from the list' at POS=(21,12), so the map advertises upper case alone - yet :191 and :201 accept the lower-case forms as WHEN labels of their own. Both facts are verified legacy behaviour and are preserved rather than tidied (practice B5); SignOnService upper-cases its input unconditionally, and the asymmetry between the two programs is real. The compound guard at :187-188 is TRUE because both selection fields are now set, so the selection EVALUATE is entered. 'd' fails WHEN 'U' at :190, WHEN 'u' at :191 and WHEN 'D' at :200, and matches the FOURTH clause, WHEN 'd' at :201, whose body is shared with :200 and runs at :202-209: 'COUSR03C' into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, WS-TRANID into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, WS-PGMNAME into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, and MOVE 0 TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT. The program context therefore ARRIVES AS 1 - the CDEMO-PGM-REENTER that made :121's RECEIVE happen at all and sent :122 down its WHEN DFHENTER arm - and DEPARTS AS 0, which is the assertion that this transfer really did reset the pseudo-conversation. WHEN OTHER at :210-214 is last and is not reached here; case16 drives it. THE XCTL AT :206-209 TRANSFERS CONTROL, so nothing after it executes. :218-222's USRIDINI test, :224's cursor move, :227's MOVE 0 TO CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM, :228's PERFORM PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD and :230-232's USRIDINO blanking are all unreached, which is why CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM leaves holding the 1 the payload carried rather than the 1 a freshly built page would have computed. That is a NEGATIVE arithmetic assertion (gate G28): not one of the four sites - :304, :309-310, :320-321 and :358 - fires, and a translation that paged forward anyway would have arrived at the same number by an entirely different route. No STARTBR, no READNEXT and no ENDBR is issued at all (gate G47), neither INITIALIZE-USER-DATA nor POPULATE-USER-DATA runs, and SEND-USRLST-SCREEN is not reached - so 'sends' is empty rather than absent, and expectedMessages is empty because no map is painted and the three DISPLAY sites at :608, :642 and :676 are all WHEN OTHER arms of a browse this case never starts. In the stateless projection the transfer becomes the response's nextProgram and the client issues the follow-up call (gate G40): there is no server-side forward, no redirect chain and no session affinity. nextMapset and nextMap stay unset, because COUSR00C names neither - it never writes CDEMO-LAST-MAP or CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET. The received screen, the AID and the whole 194-byte area travel in the payload and nowhere else (gate G37, rule R6). CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG and CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED are how COUSR03C learns which user to delete, so both are pinned explicitly and the lower case is pinned specifically: 'd', and USER0005. NOTHING IS DELETED HERE. COUSR00C opens USRSEC for browse alone - app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD grants ADD, BROWSE, DELETE, READ and UPDATE, and this program uses browse only - and on this path it does not even browse; the delete itself belongs to COUSR03C and to its own parity cases. The file is therefore pinned untouched and unmutated: all twenty-five rows at their 80-byte width, row 0 decoded field by field as well as pinned whole, and expectedDatasets carrying the row count no row expectation can state on its own. SEED. USRSEC has no ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds nine and none of them is a security-user file - so its rows are always inline. Rows 1 to 10 are VERBATIM in-stream records of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 at their in-stream width of exactly 57 characters. Rows 11 to 25 are the fifteen SYNTHESIZED extension records, byte-identical to the twenty-five-record seed of case05, case06, case07, case16 and case20: one 25-record file per folder rather than two, so that ZUSER001 names the same record in every case that reaches it. The twenty-five records matter to this case specifically, because CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG arrives as 'Y' and a ten-record file could not honestly carry that flag. No row is pre-padded: the 23-byte shortfall is the absent SEC-USR-FILLER and it is carried to 80 once, at seed time, by the single USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation declared below, which the harness and FieldDiffer own. SEC-USR-PWD stays the plaintext eight-character literal the legacy design stores and compares (practice B6); hashing, masking or omitting it would change what this contract asserts. DECLARED GAP (practice B12). With this case in place all four labels of the selection EVALUATE are pinned by a parity case of their own - 'U' by case13, 'D' by case14, 'u' by case15 and 'd' here - so the twin-clause gap the plan anticipated does not arise, and the user package's unit suite drives all four again under gates G49 and G50. What IS declared instead is the ELSE at :220-222: no parity case now anchors a browse on a start key the operator typed into USRIDINI, because gate G15 fixes the budget at exactly twenty cases per program and this case spends its slot on the tenth selection arm, which no other case reached. That branch is driven by the user package's unit suite instead, which exercises a typed start key repositioning the browse and the page count restarting behind it. Recorded rather than omitted silently. NOT APPLICABLE AND NOT FABRICATED: gate G32, because COUSR00C contains no GO TO; gate G35, because it contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and no MOVE ... TO RETURN-CODE, which is also why expectedReturnCode is 0 here and on all twenty cases, every path ending at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :141-144 or at an XCTL before it; and gate G43, because it has no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC. Gate G38's REENTER side is what this case drives, and COUSR00C does NOT copy CSSETATY - its COPY list is exactly COCOM01Y, COUSR00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so there is no runtime DFHRED and no '*' overwrite to expect, and ERRMSG's red is static in app/bms/COUSR00.bms. USRSEC is addressed by its binding key throughout and never by a dataset name (gate G46). RULE R1: the plan mandates the class name UserMenuController, but app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:5 reads 'Function : List all users from USRSEC file', app/bms/COUSR00.bms paints 'List Users', and README.md records CU00 the same way - the name comes from the plan and the behaviour from the source, and nothing here expects menu-shaped behaviour. The dead WS-USER-DATA array at :56-64 is left unmodelled for the same reason (practice B5). PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here was DERIVED BY STRUCTURED READING of app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:151-181, :187-188 and :200-209, cross-checked against app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 whose sixteen spans sum to 160 and beneath which :67-75 adds the 34-byte CDEMO-CU00-INFO of 8+8+8+1+1+8 - COTRN00C's equivalent is 58 and is not copied here and NavigationContext stays exactly 160 for all seventeen controllers - app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 whose 8+20+20+8+1 = 57 plus the NAMED SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) make 80, app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY from which the field names and every width are taken from the xxxI items alone since the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are length, flag and attribute metadata and never payload (gate G9), and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl whose :35-44 supply the seed and whose :48 DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) and :64-66 IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80) fix that width independently (practice B11). It was NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program: executing it is impossible in this environment, which has no z/OS or CICS runtime, whose COBOL compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, and which is missing the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA (risk R-D). Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted (AAP 0.7.6 and 0.9.11); the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate are all preserved. The code page is named US-ASCII explicitly and never defaulted, and the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the source's own version stamp rather than an invented instant - both carried here for uniformity, since a path that transfers before its first send paints no header for POPULATE-HEADER-INFO to stamp (practice B8, practice B7).
